name: Brachydactyly-elbow wrist dysplasia syndrome
aliases: Brachydactyly with elbow and wrist dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and radiological diagnostic criteria for Brachydactyly-elbow wrist dysplasia syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of brachydactyly characterized by shortening of the fingers
Radiological evidence of elbow joint dysplasia including hypoplasia or malformation of the distal humerus
Radiological abnormalities of the wrist bones including carpal bone hypoplasia or fusion
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Normal cognitive development without intellectual disability

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of brachydactyly with radiological confirmation of elbow and wrist dysplasia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by radiographic imaging; genetic testing may assist but is not definitive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormal distal phalanx morphology of finger

imaging: Radiographs showing brachydactyly with shortened phalanges
Elbow X-rays demonstrating distal humerus dysplasia
Wrist imaging revealing carpal bone hypoplasia or fusion

distinguishingFeatures: Brachydactyly primarily affecting metacarpals and metatarsals
No associated elbow or wrist dysplasia
Progressive joint fusions including elbows and wrists

redFlags: Progressive joint contractures leading to severe functional impairment
Signs of neurodevelopmental delay (uncommon in this syndrome)
Severe limb deformities causing vascular or neurological compromise
